planting.note: Plant offsets or container-grown divisions in spring in gritty, humus-rich, sharply drained soil in partial shade, ideally in a pot under a cold frame or alpine house where the fragile farina is protected from rain.

directions: A classic grey-edge show auricula, 'Grey Lag' carries fragrant black-ground flowers edged in powdery grey farina surrounding a pure white centre and yellow eye, held above spoon-shaped, toothed, silvery-coated foliage. Grow in gritty, loam-based compost that is moist but well-drained, in full sun to partial shade, and keep flowers and leaves dry overhead to protect the farina from rain spotting. Best grown in pots in an alpine house, cold frame, or on a traditional auricula theatre. Divide and repot offsets every one to two years after flowering to maintain vigor and true show form.

planting.note: Plant offsets or container-grown divisions in spring in gritty, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Border auriculas are generally more garden-tolerant than show types but still resent winter waterlogging.

directions: A Border-class auricula with heavily mealy, farina-dusted foliage and deep red flowers centered on a white paste ring and yellow eye, 'Craig Dhu' is one of the more robust and fragrant auricula types, tolerating open garden conditions better than exhibition show types. Plant in gritty, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade with protection from the hottest midday sun. Divide congested clumps every one to two years after flowering to keep rosettes vigorous.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist but well-drained, humus-rich soil in full sun to partial shade; rosettes multiply quickly into mounds that can be lifted and divided.

directions: 'MacWatt's Blue' forms rosettes of spoon-shaped, serrated, mealy-coated pale green leaves topped in spring by sturdy stems carrying bunches of rounded, rich purple-blue flowers with a creamy eye. Grow in moist but well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; new spring growth is covered in attractive powdery farina just before flowering. Removing spent flowerheads often forces a second flush of bloom, and the quickly multiplying rosette mounds are easily increased by division.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in chalk, clay, loam, or sandy soil that is moist but well-drained, in full sun to partial shade.

directions: A Border-class auricula bearing fragrant, bright lemon-yellow flowers with wavy-edged petals and a small white centre, held above compact rosettes of spoon-shaped, toothed, rich green foliage. 'Paradise Yellow' is a robust, garden-tolerant auricula suited to rockeries and containers as well as pots, adapting to a wide range of soil types as long as drainage is adequate. Divide congested rosettes every couple of years after flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in partial shade; this double-flowered cultivar is exceptionally cold-hardy.

directions: A pale lemon-yellow double auricula bred by Lynne Lawson at Barnhaven, 'Lemon Sorbet' carries multiplied, buttery-toned petals on sturdy stems above neat evergreen rosettes. Grow in well-drained soil in partial shade; it is suited to borders, containers, rockeries, and troughs and tolerates winter cold exceptionally well for a double auricula. Divide offsets every one to two years to keep clumps vigorous.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, with shelter from the hottest midday sun; excellent as a container and cold-greenhouse plant.

directions: A strong-growing, soft grey-leaved show auricula, 'Cuckoo Fair' produces fragrant, vibrant dark purple-blue flowers with a white centre and yellow eye in late April into May, above spoon-shaped, toothed, pale green rosettes. Site in a sunny, well-drained spot with shade from the worst midday heat; it is well suited to container culture and as a cold greenhouse plant. Divide offsets every one to two years after flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in gritty, well-drained soil in partial shade, ideally in a pot kept dry overhead to protect the flower's edge coloring.

directions: A Fancy-class show auricula with a purple flower body set off by a grey-green edge, 'Helen Barter' is grown by specialist auricula nurseries for exhibition and collector use. Plant in gritty, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade, keeping the farina-dusted foliage and flower faces dry overhead. Best grown in pots under glass or on an auricula theatre, and divided every one to two years after flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist but well-drained soil in full sun; grown as much for its variegated foliage as for its flowers.

directions: Grown chiefly for its ornamental foliage, 'Beeches Variegated' (also offered under the name 'Piers Telford Variegated') has spoon-shaped, serrated rosettes irregularly splashed with yellow variegation, topped in spring by clusters of rounded orange flowers with a bright yellow eye. Grow in moist, well-drained soil in full sun; the rosettes multiply quickly into mounds that are easily increased by division, and deadheading often forces a second flush of bloom.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in gritty, well-drained soil in partial shade, kept dry overhead to protect the flower edge and farina.

directions: A Show-class green-edge auricula also known under the historic variant spellings 'Gildersome Green' and 'Guildersome Green', this cultivar carries a black-ground flower with green feathering toward the petal margins surrounding the classic pure white show centre, above a basal rosette of farina-dusted leaves. Grow in gritty, well-drained compost in partial shade, ideally in a pot under cover where the farina and petal edge are protected from rain. Divide and repot every one to two years after flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in gritty, well-drained soil in partial shade, ideally in a pot kept dry overhead.

directions: Raised by Woottens of Wenhaston, the Suffolk auricula and iris specialists, 'Ragged Canary' is a lightly fragrant Fancy-class show auricula with multi-coloured yellow flowers edged in green. Grow in gritty, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade, keeping the foliage and flower faces dry overhead to preserve the farina and petal edge. Best grown in pots under cover and divided every one to two years after flowering.
